topic: Golfer's elbow: pain on the inside of the elbow

slides.headline: Golfer's elbow isn't just for golfers
slides.sub: Inside-of-elbow pain is common in lifters, tradies and desk workers.

slides.title: What golfer's elbow is
slides.body: It's irritation of the tendons on the inside of the elbow that help bend the wrist and grip. It usually builds up gradually after a change in gripping, lifting or carrying.

slides.title: Common triggers
slides.body: A new gym program with heavy pulling, lots of tool use, carrying shopping or kids, a new sport, or long hours on a mouse can all add up. Usually it's the total load that matters.

slides.title: Ease the load, don't rest it all
slides.body: Try a lighter grip, lifting straps on heavy pulls, and splitting up repetitive tasks. Complete rest often calms it, but the tendon usually needs gradual loading to build capacity.

slides.title: A simple strength start
slides.body: Wrist curls with a light dumbbell, palm up, done slowly: 3 sets of 10 to 15 every second day. Mild discomfort that settles by the next day is usually OK.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Numbness or tingling into the ring and little fingers, sudden pain after a fall or heavy lift, swelling, or pain that keeps building despite easing off is worth getting checked.

caption:
Inside of your elbow aching every time you grip, lift or pull?

That's often golfer's elbow, and you definitely don't need to play golf to get it. Heavy pulling at the gym, tool use, carrying kids or shopping and long hours on a mouse can all add up.

Full rest often calms it, but the tendon usually needs gradual loading to build capacity again. Lighten your grip where you can, use straps on heavy pulls, and start slow wrist curls every second day. Mild discomfort that settles by the next day is usually fine.

Tingling into the ring and little fingers, or pain that keeps building, is worth getting checked.
